newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH FIRMS PREPARE TO TRANSFER TO EURO IN 1999.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH FIRMS PREPARE TO TRANSFER TO EURO IN 1999.

text.p: Big Finnish companies look set to transfer to the new Euro currency as their invoicing and accounting currency at the start of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999, a finance ministry official said on Tuesday.
"Bigger companies will start using the Euro as their home currency at a relatively early stage -- after January 1, 1999," EMU project coordinator Rauno Niinmaki said at a briefing for journalists.
"In Finland, many businesses seem keen to make the transition as soon as possible," he added.

Separately, Jussi Mustonen, director at the Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers (TT), told a seminar on Tuesday that big companies are better placed than smaller to operate in the Euro -- regardless of Finland's timetable in joining the third stage of EMU.
"But small and medium sized companies will benefit most from Finland being among the first to join EMU," Mustonen said in the text of his prepared speech.
"Joining EMU will decrease exchange rate risks and costs, lower interest rates and create a framework for stable economic development," he added.

According to a recent TT survey, 72 percent of industrial companies want Finland to be among the first to join EMU. In favour of joining at a later stage are 28 percent and only 0.1 percent think that Finland should not join at all.

Finland is expected to meet the convergence criteria for membership of EMU in the first scheduled entry wave in 1999. Parliament is due to decide late this year or early in 1998 whether Finland should join the single currency area from the beginning.
